title: AI Safety Index for Mid-Tier Labs: Extending Beyond the Top 8

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: extending governance coverage is valuable in principle, but mid-tier labs may lack sufficient public documentation for meaningful scoring. Data sparsity could undermine results.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: applying a governance assessment methodology requires understanding the FLI rubric and making judgment calls on incomplete data. Non-trivial for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone within 30 hours: assessing 10-15 labs across 15 indicators is a large undertaking that would likely be incomplete or superficial within the time constraint.

novelty.reasoning: The FLI AI Safety Index currently covers only 7-8 frontier AI developers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI, Zhipu AI, DeepSeek, Alibaba Cloud). Safe Superintelligence Inc. was explicitly excluded for not having deployed frontier models. No existing assessment extends the FLI methodology to mid-tier labs (e.g., Cohere, AI21 Labs, Stability AI, Mistral). While the idea has significant feasibility concerns (data sparsity for mid-tier labs, as noted in the score), the research question itself — whether mid-tier labs exhibit systematically different safety practices — has not been empirically addressed.

evidence: FLI AI Safety Index Winter 2025 — 8 companies assessed.
FLI AI Safety Index 2024 — 6 companies assessed.
AI Safety Index Summer 2025 — notes SSI excluded for no deployed models.
